summary: Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989 and earned a master's degree from Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2008, he pursued an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik, while also studying under the traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Collège de France under Langlès, Silvestre de Sacy, and Kieffer. A founder of the Société Asiatique, he held the Indian language chair at ENLOV/INALCO (1828–1877/1878).

Gareth Fisher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (1999–2006) and became Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University in 2008.

Gareth Sparham specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1974–1982), he completed his Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar (~1982–1989) and lectured at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1974–1979). He taught at Harvard (~1979–1985), Columbia University (~1999–2007), and the University of Chicago (~2007–2023), where he became Professor Emeritus.

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. He was mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, and served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross.

Gary Donnelly works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Liverpool (MA 2013–2014), Oxford, and the University of Manchester. He taught at Liverpool (2016–2020) and served as a temporary Lecturer in Indic Traditions at Liverpool Hope University (2023).
Gary Goh Wee Kian focuses on philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hui-Chieh Loy, Jay L. Garfield, Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder is a scholar and writer in religious and Buddhist studies who co-founded the Buddhist Peace Fellowship. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley, later serving as a professor at the University of California, Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton is an anthropologist and historian who earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) before serving as Dumbarton Oaks Professor and anthropology department chair at Harvard University (~2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Italian Indologist who studied at the University of Turin, the University of Vienna, and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair of Sanskrit at the University of Turin (from 1852) and directed its National University Library.

Gaston Courtillier was an Indologist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1897). He taught at Lycée Fustel de Coulanges (~1919–1933) and was Chargé de conférences for Sanskrit at the University of Strasbourg (1924).

Gaston Paris was a French linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez (~1856–1858) and at the École des chartes (~1858–1862). He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1895) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique from approximately 1899 to 1901.

Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and he taught Shenphen Nangwa and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima.

Gauri Viswanathan is an Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Delhi and a Ph.D. from Columbia University. She taught English at the University of Delhi (~1973–1983) and became Class of 1933 Professor in the Humanities at Columbia (~1989).

Gaurinath Sastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1954–1969), Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1958–1962), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1976–1979).
Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1885–1888) and under Bhagwanlal Indraji (~1887–1888), later teaching Bisheshwar Nath Reu.
